step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identified core input source 'FACTORY' representing 15+ factories, 6 source systems per factory, and ~4,000 data streams.
2. Identified ingestion and processing layer with 'KAFKA' (streaming ingestion) and 'EMR' (holding Flink real-time consumers and UDI batch jobs).
3. Identified storage and querying layer grouped logically inside a data layer: 'S3' (data lake storing ~30 TB), 'REDSHIFT' (data warehouse using Spectrum), and 'AURORA' (operational real-time database).
4. Identified consumer layer: 'BI REPORTS' reading from Redshift and S3, 'REAL-TIME APPS' querying Aurora, and 'EXTERNAL SYSTEMS' querying platform data via APIs.
5. Structured all data flows from ingestion down to downstream consumer analytics and operational access.

edges.notes: Factories stream real-time production data to Kafka clusters.
Flink consumers on EMR consume Kafka data streams in real time.
EMR Flink layer streams processed data directly into S3.
EMR Flink layer writes real-time outputs directly to Aurora.
Secondary EMR UDI batch transformation jobs process data recursively.
Redshift Spectrum queries data stored directly in S3.
BI Reports and ML models read directly from S3 based on specific analytics workloads.
Redshift serves data to BI reports.
Real-time factory applications query Aurora for operational data.
External systems consume platform data via APIs connected to Aurora.
